title: Month-over-Month Stream Drops
description: For each streaming show, compare its monthly stream count with the previous month that actually has data. Return one row per month where streams dropped: show_title, month (the month with the drop), streams (streams in that month) and prev_streams (streams in the show's previous recorded month). The first recorded month of each show has no previous month and must not appear. Results are ordered by show_title ascending, then month ascending.
solutionQuery: WITH with_prev AS (SELECT s.title AS show_title, st.month AS month, st.streams AS streams, LAG(st.streams) OVER (PARTITION BY st.show_id ORDER BY st.month) AS prev_streams FROM Streams st JOIN Shows s ON s.show_id = st.show_id) SELECT show_title, month, streams, prev_streams FROM with_prev WHERE prev_streams IS NOT NULL AND streams < prev_streams ORDER BY show_title ASC, month ASC
explanation: A CTE computes LAG(streams) partitioned by show and ordered by month, so each row sees the previous recorded month even when calendar months are missing (Tiny Homes skips 2024-02). The outer query keeps only rows where a previous month exists and streams actually fell. Ordering by show_title then month makes the output deterministic.
